description: Fact sheet for NadiSaathi. status: verified = official/primary page opened; secondary = news, paper, or third-party copy; unverified = could not confirm.

facts.claim: DHM's monsoon plan says the public in affected areas is alerted by SMS from Nepal Telecom and Ncell when a river reaches or is likely to reach the red (danger) mark.
facts.source_title: The Himalayan Times, 12 Jun 2019: DHM develops monsoon response plan
facts.quote: general public of the concerned areas will be alerted through SMS by Nepal Telecom and Ncell
facts.note: News report (2019) of DHM's plan; DHM site itself unreachable. Same article: 'If the water level of rivers reaches or is likely to reach the red mark'.

facts.claim: Nepal Telecom gives DHM the details of subscribers in disaster-prone areas; DHM sends them early-warning SMS via the 1155 access code, free of charge.
facts.source_title: NepaliTelecom: Nepal Telecom sending early warning SMS for coming natural disaster
facts.quote: The department then sends the early warning message to those people through 1155 access code.
facts.note: Also: 'Nepal Telecom provides the details of the people living in those disaster-prone areas to DHM.' and 'Ntc has been providing all the SMS services at free of cost.' Rivers listed: Mahakali, West Seti, Kankai, Babai, Karnali, Narayani, Bagmati, Koshi.

facts.claim: DHM sends SMS alerts to nearby settlements as soon as a river crosses its warning or danger level.
facts.source_title: Republica: DHM sending early SMS alerts to mitigate risks of floods (dated July 25, year not shown)
facts.quote: As soon as the updates show any river crossing the warning or danger level, the alerts are sent to the nearby settlements.

facts.claim: Ncell has sent flood early-warning SMS to people in flood-prone areas since 2016, and sent over 9 million SMS alerts in 2023.
facts.source_title: The Himalayan Times, 11 Jan 2024: Ncell, DHM sign MoU strengthening early warning systems to cover 13 hazards
facts.quote: Since 2016 Ncell has been disseminating flood early warning SMS alerts to people living in flood-prone areas.
facts.note: Also: 'Last year alone in 2023, the company disseminated over 9 million SMS alerts.' A different NepaliTelecom report gives 44 lakh for 2023 (not opened); treat the count as uncertain.

facts.claim: Ncell and DHM signed an MoU on 10 January 2024 extending SMS early warning to 13 hydro-meteorological hazards.
facts.source_title: The Himalayan Times, 11 Jan 2024: Ncell, DHM sign MoU strengthening early warning systems to cover 13 hazards
facts.quote: Flood, Flash Flood, Rainfall, Thunderstorm, Windgust, Landslide, Avalanche, Snowfall,

facts.claim: In Nepal's flood EWS, the telemetry network triggers automatic SMS to chief district officers, DHM basin offices and security forces; district offices run display boards with sirens.
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: The second utilizes the telemetry system to trigger automatic SMS text messages, such that warnings are sent to chief district officers, DHM basin offices, along with security forces

facts.claim: Community-based EWS (CBEWS) trained community gauge readers to watch river levels and warn downstream communities when levels pass warning and danger thresholds; gauge readers warn by mobile phone and SMS.
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: Initially the CBEWSs trained community gauge readers to monitor river levels and disseminate warnings to downstream communities when river levels rose above the defined warning and danger thresholds

facts.claim: In Karnali CBEWS, the warning level means water reaches the top of the riverbanks at the downstream site at risk; the danger level means water overflows the banks into communities.
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: Warning Level – condition when water reaches the top of the riverbanks for the downstream site at risk
facts.note: Danger level: 'condition when water overflows the riverbanks and water enters the communities and floodplains downstream.' This is the paper's definition for Chisapani; DHM's own hydrology.gov.np legend could not be opened.

facts.claim: DHM had 286 meteorological and 170 hydrological stations (figure cited from Shrestha et al., 2014).
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: DHM now has 286 meteorological and 170 hydrological stations nationwide (Shrestha et al., 2014)
facts.note: Old figure (2014); current count not verified.

facts.claim: On 19 Oct 2021, DHM sent a mass SMS at 8 AM saying the Karnali had crossed the warning level, an hour after the gauge reader's 7 AM reading of 10.2 m at Chisapani.
facts.source_title: Nepal Red Cross Society et al.: Acting in anticipation against unseasonal floods in Nepal (case study, Oct 2021 Karnali floods)
facts.quote: 8 AM: SMS alert from DHM informing that warning level has been crossed in Karnali

facts.claim: During the 26 Aug 2026 Bhotekoshi-Trishuli flood, more than 600,000 SMS warnings went to riverbank residents of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan between 9:15 and 9:16 am (Kathmandu Post attributes them to the Flood Forecasting Division).
facts.source_title: The Kathmandu Post, 27 Aug 2026: How the Bhotekoshi flood unfolded over 10 hours
facts.quote: More than 600,000 messages were sent.
facts.note: Mongabay reports DHM's count as 679,295 residents and says it could not verify the time; the Prime Minister told Parliament the first batch went out at 9:35 a.m.

facts.claim: After the Aug 2026 flood, critics said official SMS warnings were generic and lacked exact locations, severity and instructions; DHM describes its system as threshold-based river sensors.
facts.source_title: Mongabay India, Sep 2026: Community-based warning saves lives during Nepal floods
facts.quote: threshold-based river sensors: When water crosses a preset danger level, it triggers an alert.

facts.claim: Nepal's DRRM Act 2074 (2017), Act No. 45, establishes the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) under the Ministry (of Home Affairs).
facts.source_title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074 (2017), English text with Rules 2076 (copy hosted by DPNet Nepal)
facts.quote: There shall be established a National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority under the Ministry to effectively carryout and manage disaster management activities.
facts.note: English translation hosted by DPNet; assented 2074/07/05 (22 Oct 2017), first amendment 23 Feb 2019.

facts.claim: Under the DRRM Act, every local level must set up a Local Disaster Management Committee (up to 15 members, chaired by the mayor or rural municipality chair) that develops and runs a local early-warning system and emergency operations centre.
facts.source_title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074 (2017), English text with Rules 2076 (copy hosted by DPNet Nepal)
facts.quote: Every local level shall establish a Local Disaster Management Committee consisting of such members, not exceeding fifteen, chaired by the chairperson of village body or mayor of municipality.
facts.note: Function (j): 'Develop or cause to develop an information system on disaster management and early-warning system at local level, and make them operational;'

facts.claim: Ward or municipal 'disaster focal persons' are NOT named in the DRRM Act 2017 English text that was checked (no occurrence of 'focal').
facts.source_title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074 (2017), English text with Rules 2076 (copy hosted by DPNet Nepal)
facts.note: The NRCS case study does mention 'DRR focal person at the municipalities' as a practice, but the Act text does not. Do not attribute focal persons to the Act.

facts.claim: hydrology.gov.np warning/danger level legend and DHM station pages could not be opened (connection refused) on the access date.
facts.source_title: DHM real-time hydrology portal (connection refused on access date)
facts.note: Any claim quoting the portal's legend or per-station thresholds is unverified.

facts.claim: CWC issues flood forecasts at 340 stations: 200 level-forecast and 140 inflow-forecast stations.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: Presently, flood forecasts are issued by CWC at 340 stations (140 Inflow Forecast Stations + 200 Level Forecast Stations).
facts.note: Basin table: Ganga & tributaries 96 level + 43 inflow = 139.

facts.claim: CWC level forecasts start when the river touches or is expected to touch the Warning Level, usually 1 m below the Danger Level.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: pre-defined Warning Level (usually 1 meter below the Danger Level, but also dependent on the threat perception of the particular location)

facts.claim: CWC alert categories: Above Normal (yellow) = between Warning and Danger Level; Severe (orange) = between Danger Level and HFL; Extreme (red) = above the HFL, the highest level ever recorded at the site.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: *Highest Flood level- The highest flood level of the river ever recorded at the place.
facts.note: Annex-3.2: 'Above Normal: Yellow', 'Severe: Orange', 'Extreme: Red'. Orange alerts updated 6-hourly, red 3-hourly.

facts.claim: CWC issues more than 8,000 flood forecasts every flood season and has run a 7-day rainfall-runoff advisory since 2023.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: Annually, more than 8,000 flood forecasts are being issued by CWC during flood season.

facts.claim: CWC's SOP requires CAP alerts on the SACHET platform for all level forecasts issued from divisional flood control rooms.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: CAP alerts should be issued for all level forecasts from DFCR in the Sachet platform

facts.claim: IMD's automatic weather stations and rain gauges, and IMD Flood Meteorological Offices, feed rainfall data into CWC flood forecasts.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: Automatic Weather Stations/Automatic Rain Gauges of India Meteorological Department(IMD) shall provide necessary inputs in formulation of flood forecasts.

facts.claim: SACHET is NDMA's CAP-based Integrated Alert System, built by C-DOT, for geo-targeted alerts in local languages over SMS, Cell Broadcast, radio, TV, sirens, social media, web and apps.
facts.source_title: PIB, 31 Aug 2022: C-DOT and NDMA organise All India Workshop on CAP based Integrated Alert System - SACHET
facts.quote: over all available communication media including SMS, Cell Broadcast, Radio, TV, Siren, Social Media, Web Portals and Mobile Applications
facts.note: As of 31 Aug 2022: 'The system is already operational in 34 States and UTs. More than 75 Crores SMSes have already been sent by the system'.

facts.claim: The SACHET portal describes itself as part of India's CAP project; SMS alerts come from the header XX-NDMAEW. Alert sources shown include IMD and CWC.
facts.source_title: SACHET - National Disaster Alert Portal (NDMA)
facts.quote: User needs to be attentive when disaster alerts are received via SMS from the header XX-NDMAEW.
facts.note: Also: 'is part of CAP(Common Alerting Protocol) project implemented in India'.

facts.claim: NDMA ran a nationwide Cell Broadcast alert test on 2 May 2026 through the C-DOT-built SACHET system.
facts.source_title: The Morung Express (IANS), 2 May 2026: Govt tests nationwide mobile emergency alert system
facts.quote: NDMA will test Cell Broadcast Alerts on 2 May 2026 in your area.
facts.note: News reports also cite 134 billion SMS sent through SACHET; another summary says 6,899 crore. Not verified at a primary source.

facts.claim: Under the Disaster Management Act 2005 (s.25), each state sets up a District Disaster Management Authority chaired by the Collector / District Magistrate / Deputy Commissioner.
facts.source_title: Disaster Management Act, 2005, Section 25 (bare act text, AdvocateKhoj)
facts.quote: the Collector or District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner, as the case may be, of the district who shall be Chairperson,
facts.note: Bare-act text on a third-party law site; the NDMA PDF copy is a scan that could not be text-searched.

facts.claim: DM Act 2005 s.30 makes the DDMA responsible for maintaining early-warning mechanisms and getting information to the public. Section 30 does not mention control rooms.
facts.source_title: Disaster Management Act, 2005, Section 30 (bare act text, AdvocateKhoj)
facts.quote: set up, maintain, review and upgrade the mechanism for early warnings and dissemination of proper information to public;
facts.note: No source opened that ties DDMA control rooms to the Act; treat 'control rooms' as practice, not statute.

facts.claim: To send SMS over local routes in India, senders must register their use case and message templates with TRAI through a DLT portal and send with the Entity ID and Template ID.
facts.source_title: AWS End User Messaging SMS: India sender ID registration process
facts.quote: To send messages using local routes, you must first register your use case and message templates with the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) through a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) portal.
facts.note: AWS documentation; TRAI's own site (cms.trai.gov.in) refused connections on the access date.

facts.claim: Bihar's Water Resources Department calls Bihar India's most flood-prone state, with 76% of north Bihar's population under recurring flood threat; 68,800 of 94,163 sq km (73.06%) is flood-affected.
facts.source_title: WRD Bihar, Flood Management Improvement Support Centre: Flood history
facts.quote: most flood-prone State, with 76 percent of the population, in the north Bihar living under the recurring threat of flood devastation

facts.claim: Bihar's flood-affected area (68.80 lakh ha) is about 17.20% of India's total flood-prone area.
facts.source_title: Government of Bihar, State Transformation Cell: Flood / Water Resources page
facts.quote: about 17.20 percent of India’s total flood-prone area
facts.note: The often-quoted '22.1% of India's flood-affected population' was seen only in secondary sources and is not verified here.

facts.claim: Chisapani (Karnali) gauge: anticipatory warning at 10 m, danger warning at 10.8 m; about 45,000 km2 drains above the gauge.
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: an anticipatory warning is issued if the water level at the Chisapani gauge rises above 10 m, with a danger warning (indicating the probability of severe flooding downstream) issued at 10.8 m
facts.note: The NRCS 2021 case study instead reports a warning level of 10.2 m at Chisapani (danger 10.8 m), so warning-level values differ by source.

facts.claim: WRD Bihar's Gandak bulletin lists Devghat (Bharatpur, Nepal) maximum discharge as 674,400 cusecs (2026). Valmikinagar barrage: design 850,000 cusecs; maximum 639,750 cusecs (2003).
facts.source_title: WRD Bihar (FMISC): Discharge and gauge forecast in Gandak basin, forecast issued 24-10-2026 12:30
facts.quote: Devghat / Gandak ... Bharatpur, Nepal ... 674400 (2026)
facts.note: Quote condensed from a table row; values exact.

facts.claim: WRD Bihar's Oct 2026 forecasts note that DHM observed rainfall and water-level data were unavailable, so WRF model rainfall was used for both hindcast and forecast.
facts.source_title: WRD Bihar (FMISC): Birpur discharge forecast / Kosi flood bulletin, forecast issued 24-10-2026 12:30
facts.quote: Due to the unavailability of DHM observed rainfall and water-level data ,WRF rainfall data have been used for both the hindcast and forecast periods.
facts.note: Same note appears on the Gandak and Bagmati bulletins. Useful context for why upstream Nepal data matters.

facts.claim: Karnali CBEWS gives downstream communities about 2-3 hours of warning from Chisapani gauge readings; a DHM-applied forecasting method raised lead time to 7-8 hours.
facts.source_title: Smith, Brown & Dugar (2017), Community-based early warning systems for flood risk mitigation in Nepal, NHESS 17, 423-437
facts.quote: The current CBEWS in Karnali offers 2–3 h of warning time to downstream communities
facts.note: Method: observed upstream gauge (CBEWS) vs. data-based time-series forecast with 5 h delay. Downstream communities are on the Nepal side (Bardiya/Kailali), not India.

facts.claim: In the Oct 2021 Karnali flood the stated lead time for anticipatory action was 4 hours.
facts.source_title: Nepal Red Cross Society et al.: Acting in anticipation against unseasonal floods in Nepal (case study, Oct 2021 Karnali floods)
facts.quote: Lead time: 4 hours

facts.claim: In Aug 2014, discharge at Chatara dropped about 17.5 hours after the Jure landslide dammed the Sunkoshi; the authors read this as the travel time from the landslide to Chatara.
facts.source_title: Champati Ray & Chattoraj (2014), Sunkoshi landslide in Nepal and its possible impact in India, ISPRS Archives XL-8
facts.quote: a reduction in discharge around 17.5 hrs after the reported time of landslide and dam formation (2.30 hrs on 2nd August 2014), which is equivalent to travel time of the water from landslide area to the gauge site at Chatara on Sunkoshi

facts.claim: Chatara is 43 km from the Kosi barrage; the same paper expected floodwater from the landslide to reach the barrage in about 20 hours, implying roughly 2.5 hours from Chatara to the barrage (derived, not stated).
facts.source_title: Champati Ray & Chattoraj (2014), Sunkoshi landslide in Nepal and its possible impact in India, ISPRS Archives XL-8
facts.quote: Considering its distance of 43 km from Kosi barrage, it was expected that the flood water would reach Koshi barrage approximately after 20 hours in the event of breach.
facts.note: The 2.5 h figure is our subtraction (20 - 17.5) and should be labelled an estimate.

facts.claim: In Oct 2026, Bihar's Deputy CM said a flood wave that had crossed Devghat, about 80 km upstream of Valmikinagar barrage, was expected to reach the barrage in about six hours.
facts.source_title: ThePrint (PTI), 11 Oct 2026: No major impact expected at Bihar barrage from Nepal flash flood: Deputy CM
facts.quote: around 80 km upstream of the Valmikinagar barrage
facts.note: Official's expectation reported by PTI, not a measured travel time.

facts.claim: Basua is 64.25 km downstream of Birpur (Kosi); Chatra Bazar 47 km and Rajabas 27 km upstream. No travel time is given.
facts.source_title: WRD Bihar (FMISC): Birpur discharge forecast / Kosi flood bulletin, forecast issued 24-10-2026 12:30
facts.quote: Basua (64.25 km d/s)

facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: Duration of forecast can be used as travel time + 1hr.

facts.claim: No published travel time was found for Bagmati (Pandheradobhan/Karmaiya to Dheng/Benibad), Chisapani to Indian stations (Girijapur/Elgin Bridge), Mahakali/Sharda, or Barahkshetra to Birpur. Treat any such value as a project estimate.

facts.claim: On 18 Aug 2008 the Eastern Kosi Afflux Embankment breached at 12.9 km near Kussha (Kusaha) village in Nepal, hitting Sunsari and Saptari (Nepal) and Supaul, Madhepura, Araria, Saharsa, Katihar and Purnea (Bihar).

facts.note: Figures vary by source (2.3M, ~3M, 3.3M). GFDRR page returned 403. Prefer 'millions' or cite the exact source.

facts.claim: One SMS holds up to 160 GSM-7 characters; with any non-GSM character (e.g., Devanagari) it holds up to 70.
facts.source_title: AWS End User Messaging SMS: SMS character limits
facts.quote: If your message contains any characters that are outside of the GSM 03.38 character set, it can have up to 70 characters.

facts.claim: In multi-part messages each part holds 153 GSM-7 characters or 67 non-GSM (UCS-2) characters; each part is billed.
facts.source_title: AWS End User Messaging SMS: SMS character limits
facts.quote: the number of characters in each message part is reduced to 153 for messages that only contain GSM 03.38 characters, or 67 for messages that contain other characters.
facts.note: Twilio confirms: 'UCS-2 encoded messages contain 67 Unicode characters.'

facts.claim: Twilio: UCS-2 uses two bytes per character, cutting the limit to 70 characters.
facts.source_title: Twilio Docs glossary: What is the SMS character limit?
facts.quote: This reduces the character length limit of the message to 70 characters: 140 bytes divided by two-bytes per character.

facts.claim: India runs a 'Flood Forecasting and Warning System on rivers common to India and Nepal', in operation since 1989; in May 2002 it was agreed to raise Nepal sites from 42 to 47 and for Nepal to send real-time data from 5 key stations on the Gandak, Kosi, Rapti, Bagmati and Mahananda.
facts.source_title: PIB (Ministry of Water Resources), 24 Feb 2003: Indo-Nepal Treaty
facts.quote: has been in operation since 1989
facts.note: Old (2003) release; current station count not verified.

facts.claim: CWC's 2025 SOP tells its Lucknow (MGD-1) and Patna (LGD-1) divisions to collect hydro-meteorological data from Nepal by wireless, e-mail or website.
facts.source_title: Central Water Commission: Standard Operating Procedure for Flood Forecasting, April 2025
facts.quote: Collection of hydro-meteorological data from neighbouring countries like Nepal (MGD-1, Lucknow and LGD-1, Patna)

facts.claim: The India-Nepal Joint Committee on Inundation and Flood Management (JCIFM) held its 14th meeting on 9-13 Mar 2022; its mandate covers flood, erosion and inundation on border rivers. The source does not mention forecasting.
facts.source_title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: 14th Meeting of the Joint Committee on Inundation and Flood Management (JCIFM)
facts.quote: management of flood, erosion and inundation issues fall within the Committee's mandate

facts.claim: The 11th Joint Committee on the Kosi and Gandak Projects met in Kathmandu from 30 Apr 2026; India agreed to provide satellite imagery requested by Nepal.
facts.source_title: News On AIR, 2 May 2026: India and Nepal to hold meeting in Kathmandu...
facts.quote: The Indian side also agreed to provide satellite imagery as requested by the Nepalese side.

facts.claim: Outlook (Aug 2026), citing a Dec 2022 Jal Shakti release, says DHM data are updated hourly in the monsoon for CWC's 24-hour forecasts from its Lucknow and Patna control rooms, and names a 'Joint Team on Flood Forecasting'.
facts.source_title: Outlook India, 27 Aug 2026: When a flood crosses a border...
facts.quote: these data are updated hourly and used in 24-hour flood forecasts
